# card-harness

Card tests on real cards. Test code only; the engine imports nothing here but `createProbe`, and card-language imports the pure `strictProblems` from `strict.ts`. Not here: `validateEffect` in card-language checks one effect at run time, `strictProblems` checks a whole grammar in a test.

## Rules for agents

<!-- hooks: written by scripts/catalog.mjs from docs/catalog-notes.json; do not edit -->
**Hooks a game calls:**
- `Scenario`: build a real position and play it in a test
- `put` + `set` + `run` + `answer`: set a position up and answer its prompts
- `cardCase`: a full-resolve card test that quotes the printed clause
- `expectNotOffered`: test that an ability is not offered
- `expectNotFired`: test that a forced effect did not fire
- `runInventory`: every printed clause is cited by a test
- `cardsCheckMain`: the game cards check of clauses and records
- `screenMain`: the screen text matches the engine
- `recordPrompt` + `recordOpened`: record each prompt shown in e2e or a simulation
<!-- /hooks -->

**What it does:** Test code for card games: a `Scenario` that builds real positions and plays them, a delivery check, an inventory of printed clauses, spec rows, and a strict validator.

**You must:**
1. Use it in tests only; the engine imports nothing from it but `createProbe`.
2. Give `Scenario` a `ScenarioGame` over the game's `GameRules` (`rules`, `content`, `start()`, `put`, `probe`), or a `ScenarioPort` for a game with its own engine; `run()` with tasks needs `push` and `put` needs `put`, or it throws.
3. Build the position with `put`, `set` and `run`, then `answer(...picks)`; an `answer` refused by the engine throws with the open prompt and options printed.
4. Use `{ strict: true }` for scripted runs: `script(...)` queues answers, `check(label, fn)` fails mid-run, and `done()` fails on a leftover answer, an open prompt or equal entries in `effects(state)`.
5. Use `sc.cast('kind')` to narrow the open prompt; it throws naming the kind found.
6. Run `runInventory` from a game script: every piece of the game's language must be cited by a test file or sit in `baseline`; exit 1 when the report is stale, a piece is uncited, or the baseline lists one cited or gone.
7. Import `literalsOf` / `keysOf` / `nodesOf` from `kit/card-harness/literals`; they need `typescript`.
8. Pin a known bug as `it.fails('EXPECTED FAILURE: ...')`, never delete the test.
9. Trace only the content the engine reads to play: walking `.registry` with `Object.values` marks every id looked up.
10. Write each full-resolve card test as `cardCase({ clause, printed, ar }, fn)` from `kit/card-harness/cardCase` (it imports vitest; the index does not): `printed` the clause's text word for word, and `clause`, `printed`, `ar` as string literals, since `runInventory` reads them from the file's text. `title` adds words after the clause id (`poor`, `IX-03 …`).
11. To count only quoted tests, give each clause its `text` and the inventory the `rulings` ids: such a clause is cited only by a `cardCase` whose `printed` equals `text` and whose `ar` is in `rulings`; any other `cardCase` of it fails `<clause>: quote differs`.
11b. (K663) `printed` may be a `const` of the same file (one level: a string literal, or a template without `${}`; comments are ignored, and a name declared more than once in the file does not resolve); an import, a computed value or any other expression fails as `<clause>: printed is not a literal or a same-file const: <name>`, not as "quote differs". `mixed: true` on the inventory input (opt-in): a clause with `text` that has a `cardCase` is quote-checked as in rule 11, and every other clause is cited by an `it()` title naming its id; without it nothing changes.
12. Give each interaction row as a piece of kind `interaction` (`IX-nn`, its `cards` and `records`); only a test title (an `it` title or a `cardCase` title) cites it, else `interaction IX-nn has no test`. Pass `interacting: interactionNeeds(records, { modifier, lasting, limited })` (every modifier and lasting record, each card with several limited records): an id in no row's `cards` or `records` fails `<id> is in no interaction row`.

13. Build a game's `cards:check` with `cardsCheckMain(process.argv.slice(2), input, console.log, realRecordIo(fs))` (`./cardsCheck` or the index; Node only) and exit with its code. `input`: `faces` (`{ card, text, clauses? }`, the printed text with its ' ¶ ' marks), `catalogue` (docs/cards/catalogue.json), `records` (`{ id, clause, ...restriction keys, why? }`), `open` (content/open-clauses.json, `{ clause, reason }`), `keys` (the grammar's restriction keys), `words` (content/restriction-words.json: `"<key>:<value>"` to printed phrases), `rulings` (AR ids), `arMap` (`{ id, ar, split? }` per pattern), `readings` (`parseReadings` over every docs/cards/readings/*.md), `batch(id)` (its clause ids); optional `lasting`, `durationKey` (`duration`), `whyKey` (`why`), `exceptions` (`{ id, key, ar }`), `shape`, `wording` and `allowShape` (K509, see `patternProblems`), `baseline` (K513: a path, or `--baseline <path>`; a file of allowed problem lines `<part>: <problem>`, `#` comments and blanks ignored; a problem not in it fails, so does a line no longer found ("remove it from <file>"); `--write-baseline` writes today's lines and exits 0; needs a `RecordIo` with `read` and `write`; `NOTE` lines never count; without a baseline the output is unchanged).
14. The four parts are also pure functions, each returning its problem lines: `clauseProblems` (rejoin, sentence or paragraph end, count, orphans both ways, open clauses need a reason), `restrictionProblems` (each restriction has its words in its clause or a `why` naming a ruling; each printed word has its restriction; a `lasting` record has a duration; an exception cites a known ruling and matches something), `patternProblems` (one record shape per pattern unless its AR-map row has `split`; an encoded pattern needs a row that is not `not read`; K509 opt-ins: `wording: true` (key = the clause text with numbers outside `{...}` icon codes as N, so `{d6}` and `{d8}` differ) or `wording: (clause) => key` compares shapes only among clauses with the same key and names the key and the clashing clauses; `allowShape(clauseId, records)` returning a reason leaves that clause out of the comparison, e.g. a line another line on its card changes with "instead"; `patternNotes(input)` lists `<clause> excused: <reason>` and `cardsCheckMain` prints each as a `NOTE` line that does not change the exit code; without them the output is unchanged), `readingProblems` (the last line per encoded clause is `ok` with the hash of its records now (`recordsHash`), or `ambiguous` citing a ruling).
15. Never write docs/cards/readings/<batch>.md by hand: `--record <batch> --pr <n>` takes the PR's last comment holding verdict lines (`<clause> | ok|wrong|ambiguous|render-gap | <note>`), and fails (writing nothing) on a line naming no clause of the batch, a batch clause with no line, or no such comment; it also refuses on the default branch (`main`, `master` or origin's HEAD), with anything staged, or with other changes to the readings file; else it writes the file with a hash per clause, then `git add` and `git commit -- <file>` (that file only) and `push`; a re-run with the same verdicts prints `readings unchanged` and exits 0. A lasting record's duration needs printed words or a ruling even when `durationKey` is not in `keys`; a key holding `undefined` does not change the hash. In tests pass a fake `RecordIo`, never `realRecordIo`.
16. `--list-restrictions <batch> [n]` prints the batch's `n` (10) clauses with the most restriction words: `<clause> <count> [words] <text>`.
17. For `cards:catalogue`, split and group with `splitClauses(text, lead?)` (first at ' ¶ ', then before each match of `lead`, a lookahead), `numberClauses(card, faces, lead?, from = 1)` (`<card>#<n>` across the faces in order), `maskClause(text, names)` and `groupClauses(clauses, names)` (numbers to `N`, names to `NAME`); never retype a clause. Write `docs/cards/catalogue.json` as the `Catalogue` type (`summary.clauses`, `patterns[{ id, clauses[{ id, card, text }] }]`, `oneOffs` of clauses, `interactions[{ id }]`; more keys allowed) and check it with `catalogueProblems`.
18. Build a game's `cards:screen` (K489) as `screenMain(input, console.log)` (`./screen`) and exit with its code. `input`: `faces` (`{ id, text }` the pack's printed text), `zoom` (the zoom's text function, icons left as `{code}`), `icons` (code to label), `clauses` (`{ id, text }`), `prompts` and `opened` (take both from `Delivery.screens` and `Delivery.opened`, filled when the game's `DeliveryGame` gives `clauseOf(prompt)` (the clause that opened it) and `screen(prompt)` (the words shown, or null to leave it unscanned)); optional `syntax` (`['{', '}']`) and `strip`. Run the card tests first and hand their `screens` and `opened` to the script (a file), or the scan sees none. It prints `zoom <face>: differs at word N` (N is 1-based and counts words after `plainWords` from plain-text: NFKC, curly quotes and dashes made plain, `¶` dropped, split on white space; a longer or shorter zoom differs at the first missing word), `icon <code> has no label` (every code in `icons` or used in a printed text), `prompt for <clause>: no amount` (the clause prints a number and the prompt shows none of its numbers) and `<clause> opens a prompt no test scanned`.
19. (K496) A prompt entry in `prompts` may carry `screenOptions` (the option labels shown) and `engineOptions` (the engine prompt's options), with `label` in the input turning an engine option into its label (default `String`); both given, they must match one for one after `plainWords`, else `prompt for <clause>: option "<x>" on screen, not in the engine` or `prompt for <clause>: engine option "<x>" not on screen`. Pass neither and nothing changes. A custom verb's words must go through card-language's `describeEffect`, so `describeCheck` compares them with the printed clause; a handler that prints its own text outside it is not checked.
20. (K497) Feed `cards:screen` from a played game: in e2e or simulation runs call `recordPrompt(file, { clause, shown, screenOptions?, engineOptions? })` per prompt shown and `recordOpened(file, clause)` per opened text (JSON lines appended to `file`; Node only), then `readScreenLogs([files])` gives `{ prompts, opened }` for `screenProblems` / `screenMain`; a recorded prompt with no amount fails like one from `Delivery`. A game that passes `prompts: []` never runs the prompt checks.
21. (K497) Known `<id> is in no interaction row` findings go in a JSON map you read and pass as `interactingPending` (id to the fix that clears it): they print `<id> is in no interaction row (pending: <fix>)` and do not fail; an entry that is no longer a finding fails as `stale pending entry: <id>`.
22. (K497) Read the restriction words from `wordsPathOf(argv)` (`--words <path>`, default `RESTRICTION_WORDS_PATH` = `content/restriction-words.json`); `cardsCheckMain` given `--words <path>` and a `RecordIo` with `read` (`realRecordIo` has it when `fs.readFileSync` is passed) loads that file as `words`, else it exits 1; with no `words` in the input and no flag it loads `RESTRICTION_WORDS_PATH` through `io.read` when the file exists; `--list-restrictions` and `--record` take `--words` too. `recordPrompt` makes the log folder; `readScreenLogs` skips an unparsable line and names it in the returned `warnings`.
23. (K415) Turn the depth gate on by marking clauses `conditional` (true: it has a condition or a cost; the game decides which) or with `depth: true` on the inventory input; without either, coverage counts as before.
24. (K415) With the gate on, a clause counts as covered only by a full-resolve test: an `it`/`test`/`cardCase` whose title names the clause id (not followed by ` poor`) and whose body calls `expect…(`, `assert…(` or `.should` itself, outside strings and comments. A test under `.skip`, `.todo`, `.skipIf` or a skipped `describe` covers nothing.
25. (K415) Give each conditional clause a test titled `<clause id> poor` (a `cardCase` with `title: 'poor'` is one) whose body calls `expectNotOffered` or `expectNotFired` directly; a helper of yours wrapping them does not count. The poor test never covers the full resolve, nor the reverse.
26. (K415) A player choice: `expectNotOffered(sc, id, attempt?)` fails when an enabled option `id` or a prompt naming `id` (a top-level string field) is open now or was at any step of `sc.history`, when taking it is not refused (`attempt`, default `sc.answer(id)` in `withRewind` while a prompt is open; refused = returns false or throws the engine's refusal), or when state or events move. A forced effect: `expectNotFired(sc, id, act?, same?)` fails when any event names `id` (after `act`), when a prompt is open, or when `act` changed the state (`same` projects the part that must not move). Set the condition false or the cost unpayable first; never a test that the effect "resolves to nothing".
26b. (K648) `expectNotOffered` counts only the engine's refusal as refused (engine-core's `IllegalActionError`; the predicate sees the innermost `cause`, the error first thrown, never `Scenario.answer`'s `Answer [...] refused:` wrapper): any other throw inside the attempt (a crash) fails it as `taking <id> crashed instead of being refused: <error>`; a game on its own engine passes its refusal: `{ refused: (e) => e instanceof MyRefusal }` when its engine throws or returns a refusal class of its own, or `{ refused: (e) => /not legal|refused/i.test(String(e)) }` (its refusal's words) when it refuses with a plain `Error`; such a game must pass one, or its correct not-offered tests fail. A strict `Scenario`'s `answer` with no prompt open throws a plain `Error`, not `IllegalActionError`, so it is reported as a crash: intended.
27. (K415) `runInventory` reports kind `clause` and kind `poor` per clause, and `## Depth by family` (`family` on the clause, default `clauses`: clauses, conditional, full resolve, poor test, baseline); it exits 1 on `clause:<id> has no full-resolve test`, `poor:<id> has no poor test`, and on `<path> › <title>: its body asserts nothing` or `… calls neither expectNotOffered nor expectNotFired` (not counted) unless that clause's key is in the baseline. Adopt family by family: list the other families' `clause:<id>` and `poor:<id>` in `baseline`; an entry now covered fails as stale.

28. (K532) A clause in `cards:screen`'s `clauses` may carry `amounts`: a list of the numbers of its text that are amounts (an empty list: the prompt needs none), or `'counted'` (worked out at run time: the prompt must show some number). Unset, every number of the text counts as before. A listed number must occur in the clause text (`<clause>: amount N is not in its text`); a prompt showing none of the listed amounts, or no number for `'counted'`, still fails `no amount` (K587: for `'counted'` digits inside an icon token of the shown words, `{code}` per `syntax`, are no number). A clause id listed twice with different text, `amounts` or `promptAmounts` fails `<clause>: listed twice with different text or amounts`, and its first listing is the one checked. Set it only for a condition's number, a stat line's number or a counted amount; never to hide a prompt that drops a printed amount.
29. (K587) A clause that opens more than one prompt may carry `promptAmounts` instead of `amounts`: one entry per prompt, in the order the clause opens them, each shaped like `amounts` (a list, `[]` for none, or `'counted'`; `['counted']` for a clause with one prompt), e.g. `[['2'], []]` for a first prompt that must show the printed 2 and a second that prints no number. A prompt's place is its `step` (0-based; unset = 0): `Delivery.screens` sets it from the second prompt of a clause on (counting again after `load` or a prompt of another clause; a refused answer that leaves the same prompt object open keeps the step); a recorded prompt (`recordPrompt`) passes `step` itself. Problems: `prompt for <clause>: prompt N has no promptAmounts entry` (more prompts than entries), `<clause>: promptAmounts entry N but no prompt N opened` (an entry for a prompt that never opens, when any prompt was scanned), `<clause>: prompt N amount A is not in its text`, `<clause>: amounts and promptAmounts both set`; each prompt still fails `no amount` on its own entry. Unset, the check is K532's. Same warning: never set an entry to hide a prompt that drops a printed amount.
30. (K649) In the amount checks (rules 18, 28, 29) digits inside an icon code of the shown words (`{2-energy}`, `{dmg3}`, per `syntax`) are no number shown, so an amount shown only inside an icon fails `prompt for <clause>: no amount`; when an icon carries the amount, say so with `iconAmounts` in the input: the codes (`['2-energy']`) or a pattern a code matches (`/^dmg\d+$/`; its `g` or `y` flag is ignored). A `'counted'` prompt may carry `value` (the whole number the run computed, also through `recordPrompt`): absent from the shown words it fails `prompt for <clause>: amount <v> not shown` (a negative value must be shown with its sign, `-3` or `−3`); a value that is no whole number (`'X'`) is rejected as `prompt for <clause>: value <v> is not a whole number`, so pass the number X stands for. With `value`, every other number shown that the clause text does not print fails `prompt for <clause>: stray number <n>`; without it, two or more such numbers fail `prompt for <clause>: numbers <n>, <m> shown, pass value to tell the amount` (none is guessed to be the amount). In a counted prompt an ordinal (a digit run followed by st, nd, rd or th: `2nd`) is no number, and `allowNumbers` in the input lists numbers (`'7'`) never taken as stray or patterns (`/Unit \d+/`) whose matches are left out (a card name holding a number). (K667) The patterns of `allowNumbers` are also removed from the shown words before any amount is read or compared (counted or not) and from the clause text when its printed numbers are the wanted amounts, so a card-number reference (`/card #\d+/`) is never taken as the printed amount, while a real amount next to it (`pay 3 (card #9)`, declared 2) still fails `no amount`. Without `allowNumbers` nothing changes. Pass `value` whenever the game knows it: without it a wrong number still passes when it is the only one.

31. (K650) Keep known findings in one list per check. A check takes it as `known` (`{ file, io, open?, release?, write?, ownerOf? }`): `knownGate(name, found, known, log)` (`./known` or the index), `cardsCheckMain` (`known` or `baseline` path, `--known <path>`, `openOwners`, `ownerOf`, `release` or `--release`), `screenMain` (`input.known`), `describeCheck` (5th argument; returns only the problems left) and `runInventory` (`input.known`; its io defaults to the inventory's). In the inventory the list holds every finding, `inventoryFindings(inv)`: an uncited `kind:id` (`clause:`/`poor:` depth keys included; a test not counted is filed under its clause's key), an `interacting` id in no row, `line:<id>` for an unowned printed line; `known` replaces `baseline`, `openLines` and `interactingPending` (passing one of them with it throws). File format: a text file whose first line is `KNOWN_HEADER` (`# known findings v1: <finding> @ <owner>`) has `<finding> @ <owner>` lines (the owner: the fix batch or row that clears it); a text file without that header is read exactly as the old flat format, each line a whole finding with no owner (a ` @ ` inside it stays part of the finding); a JSON map finding to owner (K497 style) reads too; `#` comments and blanks are ignored. A check fails a finding not in the list (printed as the finding), a line no longer found (`baseline lists "<x>", which is gone: remove it from <file>`), with `open` given a line whose owner is not in `open`, starts `none` or is missing (`known finding "<x>" has owner "<o>", which is not open…`; `+`-joined owners must all be open), and with `release` any line (`release: <file> still lists "<x>"`). **Without `open`, owners are not checked at all**: a line with a closed, unknown, `none` or missing owner passes, so a finding can stay parked after its fix batch closed; pass `open` (the game's open fix batches) to give that up. A check never writes: `write: true` on a check makes it print `FAIL <name>: a check never writes <file>: run the write command (writeKnownMain) on its own` and exit 1 (`describeCheck` throws). Lines are written only by the separate write command, `writeKnownMain(name, found, known, log)` (`cardsCheckMain`'s `--write-known`; for the inventory pass `inventoryFindings(inventory(input))`, for the screen `screenProblems(input)`): it adds new findings with `ownerOf(f)` (default `none`), drops stale ones, writes the header and an owner on every line (an old flat file becomes the new format), keeps a JSON file JSON, prints `<name>: <file>: N added, M removed, T lines` and exits 0. Without `known` nothing changes.
32. (K661) A game whose options, prompts or events carry no top-level string equal to the clause id (an event `{ t: 'resolved', source: 'c1', clause: 0 }` is clause `c1#0`) passes `clauseOf(x) => string | undefined` in the options of `expectNotOffered` (4th argument) and `expectNotFired` (5th, after `same`). It maps any option, prompt or event to its clause id; it is called on the prompt, on each option of a prompt and on each event itself (not on objects nested inside them; map a batch event yourself); where it returns undefined the top-level string field match applies (an option: its `id`), where it returns a string only that string counts; a throw inside it fails as `<helper>: clauseOf threw on <item>: <error>`. Without it nothing changes. Without it such a game's poor test passes though the clause fired.

33. (K664) `wording` adds to the whole-pattern shape check, it never replaces it: a non-split pattern reports `<id> has N shapes` as without it, plus the wording lines; a pattern whose AR-map row has `split` skips the whole-pattern check but its wording groups are compared (same wording, different shape is reported). Without `wording` nothing changes. A pattern that holds several shapes by wording needs `split`.
34. (K665) `restrictionProblems` walks the effect tree of a record, not only its top-level keys. A node is the record, an object with an `op`, or an object inside a step list or branch under one of the keys `effects`, `then`, `else`, `steps`, `options`, `upgraded`, `each`, `branch`, `effect` (nested lists too); other fields (filters, targets, value expressions, metadata) are not walked, so a key there is not a restriction. A restriction at any depth satisfies a printed word and is checked for its words or `why` (the record's or the node's); a `lasting` record's duration may sit at any depth. The values of the restriction keys are not walked. The walk is iterative and visits each object once, so a self-reference or a very deep tree is safe. The record shape is unchanged; top-level restrictions are found as before. Also (K665): a printed phrase matches only as a whole token run (never inside a longer word); `/`, `-` and spaces split tokens, so `UPGRADE` is found in `UPGRADE - TACTIC/ALLY` and `TACTIC/UPGRADE`; `slashJoins: true` is the stricter opt-in (a `/` joining type words blocks a match). `ignore: [/\([^)]*?\)/]` removes the span each pattern matches in a text segment (split at ' ¶ ' and line breaks) before the printed words are read, e.g. reminder text; the rest of the line is still read; default none. `paidIcon: (step) => '{gem 2}'` names the icon a step pays, and a printed phrase equal to a paid icon of any step in the tree counts as its restriction present, default none.
35. (K668) Prompt rules in `screenProblems`, all opt-in; without them nothing changes. On a prompt entry (`ScreenPrompt`, also through `recordPrompt`): `line` (the clause line it quotes), `raw` (the text as written, before any stripping; it replaces only `shown` for the rule-id check), `path` and `card` (the record path that opened it), `payers` (the players who pay: the shown words must name each), `choices` (a choice of lines: `{ label, raw?, path?, card?, clause? }`). Rule 1 (on for a prompt with `line`, or for every prompt with `quote: true`, when a prompt without `line` fails): `line` must be the clause's whole printed words after `plainWords` and the shown words (`shown` and `screenOptions`) must hold them whole, else `prompt for <clause>: does not quote its printed clause`. `whoPays: { shared, says, ignore? }` (patterns, the game's data): a clause whose text matches a `shared` pattern, after `ignore` spans are removed, or a prompt with `payers`, fails `prompt for <clause>: does not say who pays` unless its shown words match a `says` pattern (or name each payer); it covers every clause; a `says` pattern matching any text of `BARE_YOU` (texts with a bare "you" that name no payer) fails `whoPays: pattern <p> accepts a bare "you"`. `ruleIds` (patterns read in `raw` (default `shown`), `screenOptions` and the `engineOptions` labels together, with `ENGINE_WORDS` (`[custom x]`, `Engine:`, any case) always added; `names` are exact texts, card names, removed first): `prompt for <clause>: rule id in the prompt text`. `handlers` (`{ id, clause, text }`, a hand-written handler's sentence): it must equal its clause's printed words, `prompt for <clause>: handler <id> text is not its printed clause`, or `handler <id>: unknown clause <c>`. `records` (`{ clause, path, card? }`): a prompt with `path` is credited to the clause of the longest record path at or above it, of the same card when both name one; no match keeps its own clause; every other check then reads the credited clause. `choices` are checked per option and as a whole: each option is a prompt of its own clause (by its `path` with `records`, else its `clause`), its label its shown and raw words, and the choice prompt's `line` (when set) and shown words must hold that clause whole; an option of no clause fails `prompt for <clause>: option "<label>" is no clause's`; the choice prompt itself is still checked for rule ids (its shown, options and engine options) and who pays, never for amounts. `strictLog: true` fails `no prompts recorded: run the card tests first`, `no opened clauses recorded: run the card tests first` and `logged clause <id> is in no clause`.
36. (K668) Feed the scan from every card test: `recordCardPrompts({ entry, file?, clause? })` from `kit/card-harness/promptRecorder` (it imports vitest; run it in a `setupFiles` file) sets `Scenario.onPrompt`, called with each prompt left open after a step of any `Scenario`; in a test whose title starts with the clause of a `cardCase` (or matches `clause`), it records `entry(prompt, sc)` (the words shown, `line`, `raw`, `path`...; null leaves it out) once per prompt of each scenario with `recordOpened` and `recordPrompt` to `file` (default `promptLogOf(<test file>)`: one file per test file in `PROMPT_LOG_DIR`, `test-results/card-prompts`); it returns the undo, which puts back the hook that was set before. Put `kit/card-harness/clearLog.ts` in `setupFiles` too: before each test file runs it clears that file's own log (`clearThisFileLog`; `clearPromptLog(file)` clears one file), so a re-run file never keeps old lines and other files' logs stay. Then hand `readScreenLogs(promptLogs())` to the scan with `strictLog: true`.
37. (K669) `describeCheck(cards, describe, validate?, tokens?, known?, options?)`, `options` all opt-in (without them nothing changes). `raw: { allow?: string[] }`: a reading holding a camelCase word, a snake_case or dotted key, an `AB-12` id, a `x#1` id, an empty bracket (`{}`, `[]`, `()`) or a stand-in number such as 99 fails `<id>: generated reading holds raw "<w>"`, `... an empty bracket` or `... stand-in number 99`; text inside `{}` or `[]` is not read, and `allow` lists the words the game keeps. `accepted: { <finding line>: <reason> }`: a listed line is dropped; a line that no longer occurs fails `stale accepted line: <line>`, an empty reason fails `accepted line has no reason`. `tokensOnly: true`: only the icon codes (in `{}` or `[]`) and the numbers are compared, both ways, with no word-for-word line, so a game need not filter the kit's lines by their text. `parseReadingFiles(texts)` (`./cardsCheck` or the index) parses several readings files in the order they were recorded (by the `PR #n` each names, stable; a file with none keeps its place), so `readingProblems`, which reads a clause's last line, never lets an older verdict override a newer one; `parseReadings` itself is unchanged. Tests: `k669.test.ts`.

```ts
const io = { read: (p: string) => files[p] ?? null, write: (p: string, t: string) => void (files[p] = t) }
const k = { file: 'known.txt', io, open: ['B3'], ownerOf: () => 'B3' }
writeKnownMain('my:check', ['x#1: no amount'], k, log) // the separate write command: prints "1 added"
knownGate('my:check', ['x#1: no amount'], k, log) // 0: listed, owner open
knownGate('my:check', [], k, log) // 1: the line is stale
knownGate('my:check', ['x#1: no amount'], { ...k, write: true }, log) // 1: a check never writes
```

38. (K677) A phrase in `words` (and in content/restriction-words.json) is a plain string, matched as before (any letter case, anywhere as a whole token run), or a `Phrase` object `{ phrase, case?, start? }`: `case: true` matches only the same letter case, `start: true` only at the start of the clause text (leading spaces skipped; after `ignore` removes its spans). An object, not a prefix such as `^`, because a prefix would change what an existing string means (a leading `^` is matched literally today) and the object reads plainly in the JSON file. `notPhrases` (`"<key>:<value>"` to phrases, same forms): when one is present in a clause, that key does not match there, either way (a printed phrase asks for no restriction, a restriction finds no printed source); other keys are untouched; default none. Tests: `k677.test.ts`.

```ts
const words = { 'moment:now': [{ phrase: 'Zorb', case: true, start: true }], 'optional:true': ['you may'] }
const notPhrases = { 'optional:true': ['you may not'] }
restrictionProblems({ ...input, words, notPhrases }) // "Zorb the flim." asks for moment=now; "zorb the flim." and "Then Zorb." do not; "You may not flim." asks for no optional
```

**Common mistakes:**
- (K649, breaking) A game whose prompts showed an amount only inside an icon code, or a counted prompt with two numbers the clause does not print, now fails `cards:screen`: show the amount in words, or list the icon in `iconAmounts`; drop the stray number or pass `value`.
- (K532, K587) Setting `amounts` or a `promptAmounts` entry (or `[]`) on a clause whose prompt drops a printed amount to make `cards:screen` pass: fix the prompt instead.
- Calling `answer` in strict mode with no open prompt: it throws.
- A `{ from: { state, events } }` start: the state is trusted, not validated, unless `validate` is on.
- An inventory piece listed twice: `runInventory` throws `is listed twice`.
- A cited clause only in a comment with `titleOnly: true`: it is not counted as cited.
- A spec row that still passes with its line's records removed: `cardSpecs` fails it.
- A `cardCase` with a literal `clause` but `printed: P.text` (or `ar` not a literal): counts as `quote differs`. One with no literal `clause` (shorthand `{ clause, printed, ar }`) is skipped, so its clause reads `clause:<id> is cited by no test`.
- An `ok` reading goes stale when any key of the clause's records changes (key order does not count): run `--record` again after the judge re-reads.
- `words` keys compare `String(value)`: a boolean restriction is `"optional:true"`; an object value compares as its JSON.
- (K415) A poor test whose body asserts the score is unchanged but calls neither helper: not counted, and the run fails.
- (K415) A full-resolve test that only plays the card (`sc.run(...)`) with no `expect`: not counted; an `expect` inside a string or comment does not count either.
- (K415) `it.each([...])('CL-1 %s', ...)` and other titles that are not a literal right after `it(`: not read, so they cover nothing with the gate on.
- (K415) `expectNotOffered` after the scenario offered the option earlier (then took it) fails: build the poor position from scratch, not after taking the option.
- A game without clause `text`, `rulings`, `interacting` or `interaction` pieces counts as before; the one change it sees is that a `cardCase(` call's title now counts as a test title.

- **Probe** (`createProbe<D>()`): the engine calls `probe.note(d)` (or `note(() => d)`) where it settles a choice without asking. Off in the game.
- **Scenario** (`new Scenario(game)`): the game passes a `ScenarioGame<G, W, D>` over engine-core's `GameRules<G>`: `rules`, `content`, `start()` (the state to build on), `put(s, card, where)` (a new instance, its id) and its `probe`. Then `put`, `set`, `run(...tasks)`, `answer(...picks)`, `options`, `offered`, `events`, `notes`, `observe(read, fn)`. The rules' invariants run on the built position (`{ validate: false }` to skip).
- **Engine port** (K390): a game with its own engine passes a `ScenarioPort<G, W, D>` instead: engine-core's `EnginePort` (`content`, `start()`, `apply(s, answer)` returning the state or an `Error`, `settle(s)`, `prompt(s)` with options as `{ id, enabled, why? }`, `events(s)` the whole log, optional `invariants(s, content)`, `options(s)`, `put(s, card, where)`, `push(s, tasks)` for `run`) plus `probe` and `effects`. `G` is any `PortTypes` (`state`, `prompt`, `event`, `task`, `content`); prompt ids may be strings. Every Scenario method works the same; `run()` with tasks needs `push`.
- **Delivery** (`new Delivery(game)`): the game passes a `DeliveryGame`: `load(state)` into its own session, `dispatch(picks)` through the table's path returning the settings' answers, `prompt()`, `probe`, `silentNote`, `silentAuto`. `silentChoices()` lists viewer decisions nobody was asked.
- **Inventory** (`runInventory(input, out, check, io)`): `input.pieces` is the game's language as data, `{ kind, id, cite?, cards? }` of any kind (ops, dice patterns, formulas); `clauses` the distinct printed clauses by id and card ids (never text); `tests` from `testFiles(root, dirs)`; `baseline` the `kind:id` allowed uncited. A piece is cited by a test file matching a `cite` regex (default: its id as a word) or naming one of its cards (`directOnly` turns that off). Exit 1 when the report is stale (with `check`), a piece is uncited, or the baseline lists one cited or gone.
- **Printed lines** (K83): `lines` `{ id, records }` each owned by a record or in `openLines`; `records` `{ id, verb }` checked against `routes`; all fail `runInventory`. `clauseIds([{ kind, text }])` (K26): `kind-` plus the shortest unique word prefix.
- **literalsOf(file, type, prop?)** (`./literals` or `./literals/index`, needs `typescript`): string literals of a type, or of one property of each union member, to build the piece list from the game's types. K392: `literalsOf(file, type, { keys: true })` or `keysOf(file, type)` gives the sorted property names of an untagged union (`{ gain: number } | { draw: Draw }`); a member with several keys contributes all of them. K397: primitive members (`number | { gain: number }`) are skipped, and `keysOf(file, type, { first: true })` / `literalsOf(file, type, { keys: 'first' })` return only the first declared key of each member.
- **Inventory `titleOnly: true`** (default off): a piece with no `cite` and a clause count as cited only by an id in a test title (`it`/`test`/`describe`), not one in a comment.
- **Scenario `{ from: { state, events } }`**: starts from a built state and its events; the state is trusted, not validated unless `validate` is on.
- **Checks**: `describeCheck(cards, describe, validate?, tokens?, known?, options?)` (generated reading equals the printed text word for word, `[TOKENS]` both ways); `conforms<Same<A, B>>()` (schema type equals engine type, at compile time); `report(name, errors, log)` gives the exit code. `Is<z.infer<typeof S>, T>` is `Same<DR<..>, T>` (`DR` = deep readonly), for readonly game types.
- **parseCsv(text)**: RFC 4180 reader (quotes, doubled quotes, CRLF or LF); rows as header-keyed string records, blank lines dropped.
- **Strict checks** (`new Scenario(game, { strict: true })`): `script([picks], [picks], ...)` answers the prompts that open next; `check(label, fn)` fails mid-run naming label and step; `done()` fails on a leftover scripted answer, an open prompt (strict), or equal entries in the game's optional `effects(state)`. Strict `answer` with no open prompt throws.
- **Ability trace** (`traceAbilities(registry, field = 'effects')`): pass `.registry` (the game's ability or card record, wrapped) as the content; `considered` holds ids looked up, `resolved` ids whose `field` was read to run. `expectResolved(trace, ...ids)` fails a test whose card never ran, saying looked up or never reached; `clear()` between parts.
- Walking the whole registry (`Object.values`, hashing, validation) through `.registry` marks every id looked up, and run if it reads `field`: trace only the content the engine reads to play.

- **K102 helpers**: a refused `answer` prints the open prompt and offered options (`open()`); `noPrompt()`; `changed([[label, read, delta]], fn)` lists every pair off; `literal()` or `scenarioLiteral(state, events)` gives a `{ from }` literal to paste; `withRewind(fn)` runs a branch and restores; `rulingGroups(describe)` gives `errata` and `faq` wrappers.
- **Record renderer** (K78, `renderRecords({ lines, records, templates })`): each printed line `{ id, text, open? }` followed by its records in English, one template per record `kind` (or `verb`); `say` renders nested pieces. A piece with no template prints `[render-gap kind: {json}]`, a field its template never read `[also {...}]`; `note(r)` adds a `note:` line, `kindOf`/`lineOf`/`idOf` read other shapes. Returns `text` for a reading judge (ok / wrong / ambiguous / render-gap per line), `lines` with each reading's `gaps`, and `stray` records naming no line.
- **Spec rows** (K77, `cardSpecs(name, game, rows, { describe, it })`): a row `{ line, name?, layout, act, expect }`; the game's `SpecGame` gives `records`, `play(layout, act, records, lenient)` and `check(result, e)` (a message or undefined). Two tests per row: it holds, and it fails with its line's records removed (`withoutLine`; `lenient` there: skip an answer nobody asks for). `specCoverage({ records, rows, titles?, exempt? })` gives `missing` lines (no row, no test title starting with the id) and `stale` exemptions.
- **Strict validator** (K97, `strictProblems(grammar, def, optOuts?)`): the grammar is data, `{ tag?: 'op', nodes: { kind: { keys, required?, binds?, scopes?, reads?, note? } }, ref?, given? }`; fails non-JSON values, unknown kinds, unknown keys (`wrong-place` when another kind owns the key), missing keys, a variable read before it is bound (`binds`: for later steps; `scopes`: for its children only). Opt-outs are data `{ rule, path?, citation }`; uncited or matching nothing fails. `grammarReference(grammar)` writes the workers' reference from it; `nodesOf(file, type, tag)` (`./literals`) reads kinds and keys from the engine's union, throwing when the anchor is gone.

- **cast** (K124): `sc.cast('kind')` returns the open prompt narrowed to that `kind`, or throws naming the kind found.
- **Round trip** (K114): `roundTripCards(game, [{ card, where, task? }])` puts each card in a minimal state; problems where the state is not plain JSON (`diffPaths`) or play from the JSON copy differs. `[]` passes.

Known bugs are pinned as `it.fails('EXPECTED FAILURE: …')`.
- **Content gate** (K169, `contentGate(input, log)`): the game script passes `packs` (`validate()` issues; warnings fail unless `allowWarnings`), `broken` packs each with the `code` and `severity` it must report, `generated` files compared with `readGenerated` ("stale: run `regenerate`"), and `features` `{ required, used }` (`requireAll` fails on an unused one). Returns `{ failed }`.

- **cards:check** (K488, `cardsCheck.ts`): the four parts, `--list-restrictions`, `--record` and the clause tools above (rules 13-17); `cardsCheck(input)` returns the four problem lists without logging.

## Use it in 10 lines

```ts
import { expectNotFired, Scenario } from '../kit/card-harness/index'
import { DICE_GAME } from '../kit/card-harness/fake/dice' // yours: a ScenarioGame over your GameRules

const sc = new Scenario(DICE_GAME).set((s) => void (s.dice = [2, 2, 5]))
const [twin] = sc.put('hand', 'twin') // a real card of your catalogue, in your hand
sc.run({ kind: 'play', card: twin as string })
console.log(sc.s.score, sc.events.map((e) => e.type)) // assert on state, events, options(), answer(...)
expectNotFired(sc, 'plain#9') // K415: in a `<clause id> poor` test, nothing of that id fired and no prompt is open
```

Recipe (K661, run by `k661.test.ts`): map the game's own event shape to its clause id.

```ts
import { expectNotFired, type Observed } from '../kit/card-harness/index'

const sc: Observed = { prompt: null, s: {}, events: [] } // yours: a Scenario
const clauseOf = (x: unknown) => { const e = x as { t?: string; source?: string; clause?: number }; return e.t === 'resolved' ? `${String(e.source)}#${String(e.clause)}` : undefined }
expectNotFired(sc, 'c1#0', undefined, undefined, { clauseOf }) // nothing of clause c1#0 fired, however the event is shaped
```

Recipe (K663, run by `k663.test.ts`): quote through a same-file const, and cite the clauses without a `cardCase` by test title.

```ts
import { inventory } from '../kit/card-harness/index'

const tests = [{ path: 'a.test.ts', text: "const P = 'Draw 1.'\ncardCase({ clause: 'c-1', printed: P, ar: 'AR-1' }, f)\nit('c-2 scores', () => {})" }] // yours: testFiles(...)
const inv = inventory({ pieces: [], tests, rulings: ['AR-1'], mixed: true, clauses: [{ id: 'c-1', cards: [], text: 'Draw 1.' }, { id: 'c-2', cards: [], text: 'Score 2.' }] })
console.log(inv.quoteDiffers, inv.uncited) // [] []
```

Recipe (K668, run by `k668.test.ts`): the prompt rules on a recorded prompt.

```ts
import { screenProblems, type ScreenPrompt } from '../kit/card-harness/index'

const prompts: ScreenPrompt[] = [{ clause: 'b#1', line: 'Pay 3 coins per player.', shown: 'Pay 3 coins per player.', raw: 'Pay 3 coins per player. (PAY-02)' }] // yours: readScreenLogs(promptLogs()).prompts
const whoPays = { shared: [/\bper player\b/i], says: [/\bYou pay\b/, /\bP\d pays\b/] }
const found = screenProblems({ faces: [], zoom: (t) => t, icons: {}, clauses: [{ id: 'b#1', text: 'Pay 3 coins per player.' }], prompts, opened: ['b#1'], strictLog: true, whoPays, ruleIds: [/\b[A-Z]{2,}-\d+\b/] })
console.log(found) // ['prompt for b#1: does not say who pays', 'prompt for b#1: rule id in the prompt text']
```

Recipe (K668, run by `k668.test.ts`): record every card test's prompts (a `setupFiles` file; `kit/card-harness/clearLog.ts` in `setupFiles` too).

```ts
import { recordCardPrompts } from '../kit/card-harness/promptRecorder'

recordCardPrompts({ entry: (p) => ({ shown: String((p as { text?: string }).text) }) }) // yours: the words your table shows for prompt p
```
